canonical.title: A Copenhagen weekend around a Michelin dinner

children.title: Things to do in Copenhagen
children.summary: Central walking loop day one, one neighbourhood + one museum day two, Louisiana as the single day-trip. Skip the Little Mermaid.

children.title: Michelin 2 and 3-star restaurants in Copenhagen
children.summary: Eight restaurants hold two or three Michelin stars right now — what each is, what it costs, and which you can actually book.

children.title: IT conferences and tech events in Copenhagen
children.summary: Anchor on NDC, TechBBQ, Nordic Fintech Week, Future Product Days, or GOTO; otherwise the free monthly meetups.

sources.title: Kong Hans Kælder — official
sources.claim: Kong Hans Kælder sits in a 1420 cellar off Strøget — one of two ★★ houses inside the central walking loop.

sources.title: Restaurant AOC — about
sources.claim: a|o|c occupies the basement of Moltkes Palæ near Kongens Nytorv — the other ★★ inside the central walking loop.

sources.title: Alchemist — Wikipedia
sources.claim: Alchemist is the experiential ★★ on Refshaleøen; a Refshaleøen afternoon is the natural pairing.

sources.title: Reffen — Copenhagen Street Food
sources.claim: Reffen is the Refshaleøen street-food village — the pre-dinner afternoon stop if you booked Alchemist.

sources.title: Geranium — official
sources.claim: Geranium opens reservations on a 90-day rolling window and sells through within minutes; pair with Østerbro/Langelinie.

sources.title: Koan — official
sources.claim: Koan sits at Langelinie — pair the booking with an Østerbro/Langelinie afternoon and a Juno cardamom bun.

sources.title: Jordnær — Denmark's third 3-star
sources.claim: Jordnær is in Gentofte — a 20-min S-train hop forces a quieter day around dinner.

sources.title: Geranium — booking
sources.claim: Geranium's 90-day window means firing the reservation today determines a late-September visit.

sources.title: Alchemist — official / Tock
sources.claim: Alchemist drops tickets exactly three months out via Tock against a >30,000-strong waitlist.

sources.title: NDC Copenhagen
sources.claim: NDC Copenhagen is the early-June anchor (1–4 Jun 2026) for a dev-focused trip week.

sources.title: Nordic Michelin Guide ceremony 2025–2026
sources.claim: The Nordic Michelin ceremony is at Tivoli on 1 Jun 2026 — both ★★★ booking windows have already closed for that week.

sources.title: TechBBQ
sources.claim: TechBBQ is the Aug 26–27 anchor — fire the Geranium reservation today or this week to land the late-Aug window.

sources.title: GOTO Copenhagen
sources.claim: GOTO is in the September cluster alongside Nordic Fintech Week and Future Product Days.

sources.title: noma in LA — Time Out LA
sources.claim: noma is on an LA residency through 26 June 2026, so it is not bookable in Copenhagen for this trip.

sources.title: Redzepi resigns from noma — Fortune
sources.claim: René Redzepi resigned on 14 March 2026 — noma's Copenhagen future is unclear.

sources.title: Little Mermaid — Explore.com
sources.claim: The Little Mermaid is 4 ft of bronze, consistently ranked the city's most disappointing sight — skip.

sources.title: Nyhavn food — TripAdvisor
sources.claim: Any canal-front restaurant on Nyhavn is a tourist trap — walk one block back.

sources.title: Cloud Native Denmark 2026
sources.claim: KubeCon Europe is in Amsterdam (23–26 Mar 2026), not Copenhagen — Cloud Native Denmark is the local community-grade substitute.

sources.title: Donkey Republic — pricing
sources.claim: Donkey Republic replaced the defunct city share, ~99 DKK / 24 h — bike-first city means hotel location matters less than dinner location.

sources.title: Copenhagen Card — attractions
sources.claim: The 72-h card (1,129 DKK) is worth it only if the three days include Tivoli + Louisiana + two castles — a Michelin-and-walking weekend leaves it unspent.
